entities.name: capsaicin-evoked calcium influx in DRG neurons

relationships.subject: 10Panx
relationships.evidence_quote: Pharmacological blockade of Panx1 in the DRG of rats resulted in a dose-dependent decrease of mechanical allodynia triggered by carrageenan

relationships.subject: 10Panx
relationships.object: capsaicin-evoked calcium influx in DRG neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Neuronal cells with Panx1 blockage showed lower intracellular calcium response than untreated cells after capsaicin administration.

relationships.subject: Pannexin 1
relationships.evidence_quote: Accordingly, Panx1-KO mice showed a robust reduction in mechanical allodynia after carrageenan and a lower nociceptive response to capsaicin.

relationships.subject: Pannexin 1
relationships.evidence_quote: A single dose of paclitaxel promoted acute mechanical pain in wildtype (WT) but not in Panx1-KO mice.

key_findings: Blocking Panx1 in the DRG (10Panx) or Panx1 knockout reduced carrageenan- and capsaicin-induced nociception and lowered capsaicin-evoked calcium responses in DRG neurons.
Panx1 knockout prevented acute paclitaxel pain and delayed, but did not prevent, chronic paclitaxel-induced allodynia.
